t: That the first sentence of section 1521(b)(2)(B) of the Public Health Service Act is amended to read as follows: “The period of an agreement described in subparagraph (A) shall not extend beyond July 31, 1979, or thirty-six months after such agreement has been entered into, whichever comes later.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the word "agreement" signals coordination with an outside party such as a state agency. But this section only amends the maximum duration of an agreement defined elsewhere. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.
fable.s: The period of an agreement described in subparagraph (A) shall not extend beyond July 31, 1979, or thirty-six months after such agreement has been entered into, whichever comes later.

opus.w: This amendment only changes how long an agreement under section 1521 of the Public Health Service Act can last. It does not require or allow any consultation, comment, hearing, advisory input, or legal challenge from outside parties before a federal decision. The word "agreement" appears only as a description of timing and creates no new process for outside participation.
opus.s: The period of an agreement described in subparagraph (A) shall not extend beyond July 31, 1979, or thirty-six months after such agreement has been entered into, whichever comes later.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The word "agreement" suggests a deal between the federal government and outside parties, such as health planning entities. **Why it fails:** The amendment only changes how long an existing kind of agreement can last. It doesn't create any consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue before a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely amends the statutory text to define the maximum duration of a specific type of agreement. It does not establish a process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or any other form of participation in a federal decision. The reference to an 'agreement' is substantive to the contract's terms, not procedural regarding public involvement.
qwen_chat.s: “The period of an agreement described in subparagraph (A) shall not extend beyond July 31, 1979, or thirty-six months after such agreement has been entered into, whichever comes later.”
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "agreement" implies negotiation with outside parties, thus constituting participation. However, the text only defines the duration of an agreement previously referenced in the statute; it does not describe the process of forming the agreement or require any consultation, hearing, or comment period. The amendment is purely administrative regarding time limits.
